brief: Brackets for my car's roof bars that hold my kayak for a motorway drive to the coast.

requirements.evidence: Conceptual 2-cell mockup only (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:0,1,0;full with hex-acc-bracket and 2x hex-acc-saddle cradles). No interface sized to real roof bars, no straps, no kayak present. 3D-printed plastic parts are not rated for vehicle roof loads.
requirements.requirement: Brackets that attach to car's roof bars

requirements.evidence: Two pipe saddles suggest a cradle shape but are sized for 3/4 in pipe, not a kayak hull; no hull support, padding, or tie-downs modelled.

Configurator checks fit/collisions only (meshClash clear). It knows nothing about strength, load ratings, vibration, aerodynamics, waterproofing, UV or heat. Motorway speeds impose dynamic loads and safety-critical failure risk that this system cannot verify; parts are 3D printed in user-chosen material with no rating.
requirements.requirement: Safe for motorway drive to the coast

finish.summary: Built a small conceptual cradle mockup to show bracket/saddle layout, but this cannot be used for real kayak transport. Roof-bar kayak carriers for motorway use are safety-critical and need rated, vehicle-specific hardware — do not drive with this build. Buy certified kayak roof carriers and follow car and carrier load/speed instructions.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
